previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text: (progress) I've read claude-4's morning report, queue, speed notes and the row tree. Now measuring where the overnight tokens went, per Codex session, before I say anything about cost.㊥ (can token cost come down) Yes. I measured last night from the Codex session logs, and three changes should bring the same work to roughly 40–50% of what it cost. Speed is harder: the night bought 3 new rows for about 10K credits, about 100 rows remain, and the 16,446 credits left at 13:44 UTC cover about a night and a half at that rate.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text: (where the 10K went) The window is 04:30–13:45 UTC, 10,908 credits. Nearly all the cost is context re-reading: 4,764 model calls at an average context of 155k tokens, 737M input tokens (99% cached) against 1.06M output tokens.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text: (your Lisp doubt) I think you are right that the comparison was not like for like. What a warm Lisp image buys is redefining one function without invalidating anything else. claude-4's measurements were of cache rebuilds after an edit, which is a different thing. Item 3 above is that same benefit in Python, without a rewrite.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text: (what these do not fix) The mission text expects "a relatively small generic compiler" and "not gradual declaration-by-declaration convergence". Last night's fixes were default instances, unifier reflexivity, expected-type propagation, binder instantiation for `bind` and type-argument erasure. Each is a piece of Lean's term elaborator, so the subset is turning out to be most of the elaborator, and the changes above do not alter that.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text: (a tool for next time) You said you had no before-and-after logs. The Codex logs record the credit balance at every call, so I saved the report as `/tmp/pyreg/codex_tokens.py`; it takes a start and end time and prints the table above plus the balance change.
